Native R planar trajectory acceleration, landmark distance and differential geometry

etr_native_planar_geometry.Rd

Research-stage Python-free counterparts of four public eyetrajectoriespy 1.2.0 kinematic methods. They use the standalone etr_trajectory_set object and no reticulate dependency at execution time. These are not yet independently validated numerical parity claims.

Usage

etr_acceleration_magnitude(x)
etr_distance_to_landmark(x, landmark_x, landmark_y,
                         python_boundary_mode = FALSE)
etr_signed_curvature(x, dimensions = NULL, min_speed = 0,
                     undefined_policy = c("nan", "raise"))
etr_turning_rate(x, dimensions = NULL, min_speed = 0,
                 undefined_policy = c("nan", "raise"))

Arguments

x

Native etr_trajectory_set collection on one common time grid.

landmark_x

Finite scalar or one finite x landmark per curve.

landmark_y

Finite scalar or one finite y landmark per curve.

python_boundary_mode

Logical; TRUE enables bounded frozen Python 1.2 NumPy dtype=float conversion of finite numeric-string, Boolean or mixed scalar/vector landmark coordinates and preserves the source derived-function provenance. FALSE preserves strict native finite numeric inputs and historical provenance behavior.

dimensions

Optional two distinct named channels in x/y order. Defaults to explicitly named x and y channels. No silent selection when they are absent.

min_speed

Nonnegative minimum allowed Euclidean speed. A sample with speed less than or equal to this threshold is undefined.

undefined_policy

"nan" maps the Python undefined numerical value NaN to the native R missing-data sentinel NA_real_; "raise" fails closed instead of returning a partial result.

Value

A native etr_trajectory_set with exactly one resulting functional channel named acceleration_magnitude, distance_to_landmark, signed_curvature, or turning_rate.

Details

The acceleration magnitude follows two second-order edge-aware finite differences on the original irregular common grid followed by the Euclidean norm of the first two channels. It needs at least three complete observations. Distance-to-landmark requires only two planar channels and deliberately propagates missing coordinates as NA.

Signed curvature is $$\kappa(t)=\frac{x'(t)y''(t)-y'(t)x''(t)} {(x'(t)^2+y'(t)^2)^{3/2}}.$$ Turning rate is $$\omega(t)=\frac{x'(t)y''(t)-y'(t)x''(t)} {x'(t)^2+y'(t)^2}.$$ Both quantities are undefined under the specified minimum speed, without an added denominator epsilon or smoothed heading.

The native trajectory class retains a JSON-like provenance mapping. The explicit landmark-distance Python compatibility mode preserves incoming provenance and records the source derived_function value. The Python and R object classes, all supported scalar input domains, error schemas and serialized-result representations are not fully identical. A separate independent full-domain Python/R numerical review is still required.

Examples

time <- c(0, 0.25, 0.8, 1.4, 2)
v <- array(0, c(1, length(time), 2))
v[1, , 1] <- time
v[1, , 2] <- time^2
x <- etr_trajectory_set(time, v, dimension_names = c("x", "y"))
a <- etr_acceleration_magnitude(x)
k <- etr_signed_curvature(x)
w <- etr_turning_rate(x)
d <- etr_distance_to_landmark(x, landmark_x = 0, landmark_y = 0)
